heading: Accounts, stores and staff
plain_line: Who can get into a store and act in it: the seller's account and login, staff and their permissions, and the business or organization behind one or more stores.
wont_do_removes: Seller accounts, staff and multiple stores would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly run without accounts, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1 (stores set up per place), Q3 (checks on the account) and Q6 (who may open an account).
note: The platforms file accounts, staff and organizations under different names (Shopify's account and organization, Salla's profile and staff, BigCommerce's staff accounts); no one platform's name covers them all.

heading: Store settings and administration
plain_line: Running the store itself: its name, status and opening to buyers, domain, languages, the messages it sends, and the platform's setup and status tools.
wont_do_removes: The store's own settings and messages would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q3 (what must be done before a store opens to buyers) and Q6 (what a store must give when it is set up).
note: Each platform keeps these under its own settings menu, with different names and contents (General, Store settings, عام and المتجر, Store Profile, Status).

heading: Plans, fees and support
plain_line: What a seller pays the platform and gets for it: subscription plans and their limits, fees on sales, billing, and the platform's support.
wont_do_removes: Plans, fees and support would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah would then have no plan tiers or platform fees.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q3 (what a plan unlocks), Q4 and Q5 (fees on each way of paying), Q7 (the currency the platform bills in) and Q8 (plans as a way the platform adds parts).
note: The platforms name this Plan, Billing, Store plan, الاشتراكات or Fees and Billing Terms; no one name covers them all.

heading: Products & inventory
plain_line: What a store sells and holds: products and their variants, categories, digital products, stock and the locations that hold it.
wont_do_removes: Products and stock would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without them, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Nothing: no question draws on it.
left_out: None of the eight items asks about products or stock as such. Gift cards, which Shopify files with products, bear on how buyers pay; Q5's runs add them from here where they bear.

heading: Marketing and promotions
plain_line: The seller's own tools for selling more: discounts and coupons, campaigns, affiliates and ads, loyalty, and customer wallets, cashback and store credit.
wont_do_removes: Marketing tools would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q5, where customer wallets, store credit and gift cards are ways buyers pay.

heading: Customers
plain_line: The store's customers: their records and accounts, how they sign in, their consent and personal data, reviews and questions, and their tickets and complaints.
wont_do_removes: Customer records and service would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without customer records, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, where a place's privacy and consent laws change what a store may do with customers' data.
note: Zid Assurance (ضمان زد), which Zid offers to raise customers' trust, sits here with Zid's customers.

heading: Online store and themes
plain_line: How the storefront looks and is built: themes, theme markets, pages and blogs, storefront search, and the engines theme builders use.
wont_do_removes: Themes and the storefront's design would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8, where theme markets and theme engines are ways the platform grows.
note: The platforms name this Online Store, Store design & themes, Store Design or Themes; no one name covers them all.

heading: Cart and checkout
plain_line: The buyer's cart and checkout: checkout settings and pages, abandoned carts, and the extensions and rules that change what checkout shows.
wont_do_removes: A checkout of Sharrwah's own would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without one, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q5, where checkout rules decide which payment methods a buyer sees.
note: Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce give checkout an area of its own. Salla keeps it with payments and Zid with its store settings, so their checkout is in those areas.

heading: Orders
plain_line: Orders after they are placed: their statuses, payments recorded on them, edits, returns, refunds and cancellations.
wont_do_removes: Orders would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without them, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q4 (orders paid outside the checkout) and Q5 (payments recorded on orders).

heading: Shipping and delivery
plain_line: Getting orders to buyers: shipping zones and rates, the platform's own shipping and its carriers, labels, fulfilment, and collecting cash on delivery.
wont_do_removes: Shipping and delivery would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1 (shipping set up per place), Q4 and Q5 (cash on delivery collected by a carrier or by the platform's shipping).

heading: How buyers pay: payment methods and providers
plain_line: How buyers pay: the payment methods a store offers, the providers and gateways behind them, pay-later and wallets, offline methods such as bank transfer and cash on delivery, and who approves which provider.
wont_do_removes: Taking payment from buyers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. This would undo section B's items 4 and 5, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1 to Q5.
note: Each platform files its payment methods under its own name (Payments, الدفع, Payment Methods, Payment freedom); no one name covers them all.

heading: The platform's own payment service, the seller's balance and payouts
plain_line: The platform's own payment service and the seller's money in it: Shopify Payments, Salla's wallet, Zid Pay and Zid Wallet, WooPayments; who may use it and where, verification, balances, payout timing, reserves, fees and disputes.
wont_do_removes: A payment service of Sharrwah's own, and any balance held for sellers, would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Your guard already stops any arrangement that holds sellers' money from going live without your decision.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q7. They are the main record of who holds sellers' money, which the pilot's deferred decisions turn on.
note: Each platform names its own service (Shopify Payments, Zid Pay, WooPayments) or its wallet; no one name covers them all.

heading: Financing and money products for sellers
plain_line: Money products the platform offers sellers beyond payments: business accounts and cards, loans and cash advances, and bill pay.
wont_do_removes: Lending and banking products for sellers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2 (licences and lenders by country), Q3 (who may get them) and Q5 (where a payout may go).
note: Shopify files these under Finance and Zid under تمويل زد; no one name covers both.

heading: Taxes and duties
plain_line: Taxes on sales: tax rates and registrations, automated tax, invoices and e-invoicing such as the link with Saudi Arabia's ZATCA, duties and import taxes.
wont_do_removes: Tax handling would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1 (what differs by place) and Q2 (where a tax law lands in the product, such as e-invoicing).

heading: Selling to several countries: markets, languages and currencies
plain_line: Selling to several countries from one store: per-country versions of the store (which some platforms call markets), languages and translation, and the currencies prices are shown and paid in.
wont_do_removes: Selling to several countries would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q6 and Q7.
note: The platforms name this Markets, Multi-market, الأسواق or Multi-currency; no one name covers them all. Zid's area here also holds the countries Zid serves.

heading: Where the platform operates
plain_line: Where the platform operates: the countries it serves or doesn't, the country a seller gives at sign-up, and the payment providers it suggests for each country.
wont_do_removes: Choosing where Sharrwah operates would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah must operate somewhere, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q5 and Q6.
note: Shopify, Salla and WooCommerce each list the places they serve under a different name (Unsupported countries and regions, مدعوم في, Selling locations).

heading: What may not be sold, and who may not use the platform
plain_line: What may not be sold and who may not use the platform: restricted and prohibited businesses, acceptable use, sanctions and export rules.
wont_do_removes: Rules on what may not be sold would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q3 and Q6.
note: WooCommerce and BigCommerce give these rules an area of their own; Shopify, Salla and Zid keep them in their terms or verification areas.

heading: Store Verification
plain_line: Opening a store and verifying the business behind it: the documents and checks each country requires, and the bank account that receives the store's money.
wont_do_removes: Verifying sellers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q3 and Q6.

heading: Terms, and the company a seller contracts with
plain_line: The terms a seller agrees to and the company it contracts with, which on several platforms depends on the seller's country; governing law, suspension and termination.
wont_do_removes: Published terms and contracting companies would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly operate without terms, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q6.
note: Each platform publishes its own set of agreements; no one name covers them all.

heading: Privacy and security
plain_line: Personal data and security: who controls and who processes data, where it is stored and sent, subprocessors, card security, and what the store sends back to the platform.
wont_do_removes: Privacy and security would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly operate without them, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, where a place's laws decide where data is held.

heading: Sales channels
plain_line: Selling beyond the store's own site: sales channels, marketplaces (including the platform's own, such as Zid's Mazeed), social channels, and several storefronts from one store.
wont_do_removes: Sales channels and marketplaces would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1 (storefronts per place) and Q8 (channels as parts added to a store).

heading: Point of sale (POS)
plain_line: Selling in person: point-of-sale apps, card readers, cash and the hardware behind them.
wont_do_removes: Selling in person would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q4 (cash taken in person), Q5 (card payments in person) and Q8 (point of sale as a part).

heading: B2B
plain_line: Selling to businesses: company accounts, catalogs and price lists, quotes, and payment terms such as invoices paid later.
wont_do_removes: Selling to businesses would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q4, where invoices paid on terms are arranged between seller and buyer.

heading: Apps
plain_line: Apps and extensions a seller adds from the platform's marketplace, and the services listed there.
wont_do_removes: An app marketplace would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Payment methods that come through apps, which section B's item 5 names, would go with it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q5 (payment methods that come through apps) and Q8.

heading: Build & integrate
plain_line: Building on the platform: its APIs, webhooks, access scopes and app authorization, and storefronts built apart from its themes.
wont_do_removes: Building on Sharrwah by outside developers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.

heading: Partners and services for sellers
plain_line: The platform's partners and the services sellers get through it: partner programs and their payouts, agencies, migration and growth services.
wont_do_removes: Partner programs and services would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.
note: The platforms name this Partner Program, Partners, Merchant Services or زد نمو; no one name covers them all.

heading: Analytics
plain_line: Reports and analytics on a store's sales, customers and products.
wont_do_removes: Reports and analytics would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Nothing: no question draws on it.
left_out: None of the eight items asks about reports. They show what happened in a store, and decide nothing the items ask about.

heading: AI and automation
plain_line: AI tools and automation for sellers, and AI agents that shop on a buyer's behalf.
wont_do_removes: AI tools and automation would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8, where AI features show parts introduced in stages.
note: Only Shopify and BigCommerce give these an area; each names it differently (Shopify Flow and AI-powered tools, BigAI).

heading: Mobile app
plain_line: A store's own mobile app for its customers.
wont_do_removes: A store app would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.
